message.content:
Here are some practical, everyday tips to keep your piano sounding and looking its best: | # | Tip | Why it matters | How to do it | |---|-----|----------------|--------------| | 1 | **Control Humidity** | Pianos are sensitive to moisture. Too dry and the wood cracks; too wet and the soundboard swells. | • Use a hygrometer inside the piano case.
• Keep the level between 45‑55 % RH (relative humidity).
• In winter, use a dehumidifier or a humidifier as needed.
• Avoid placing the piano near radiators, vents, or direct sunlight. | | 2 | **Regular Tuning** | Even a well‑maintained piano will go out of tune over time. | • Tune at least twice a year (or more often if you play frequently).
• Use a professional tuner for accurate pitch and temperament. | | 3 | **Keep It Clean** | Dust and grime can affect action feel and sound quality. | • Wipe down the keys, lid, and outer surfaces with a soft, dry cloth.
• Use a piano‑specific cleaner for the inside of the case if needed.
• Avoid using harsh chemicals or water on the keys. | | 4 | **Check the Action** | A sticky or uneven action can ruin playing feel. | • Lightly oil the key pins and hammers with a small amount of piano‑grade oil (e.g., 100 % pure linseed oil).
• Inspect for worn or damaged parts and replace them promptly. | | 5 | **Avoid Extreme Temperature Changes** | Rapid shifts can warp wood and damage internal components. | • Keep the piano in a room with stable temperature (ideally 18‑22 °C or 65‑72 °F).
• Use a heater or air conditioner only if it maintains a steady climate. | | 6 | **Protect the Lid** | The lid can warp or crack if exposed to moisture or heat. | • Keep the lid closed when not in use, especially in humid or hot environments.
• Use a lid protector or a small towel to absorb moisture. | | 7 | **Use a Piano Stand or Ledge** | Prevents accidental knocks and keeps the piano level. | • Place the piano on a sturdy stand or a levelled floor area.
• Ensure the base is clean and free of debris. | | 8 | **Inspect the Strings** | Broken or frayed strings can cause damage and affect tone. | • Look for any visible frays or broken strings and replace them immediately.
• If you hear a “dead” note, have a technician check the string tension. | | 9 | **Schedule Professional Servicing** | A full service catches hidden issues before they become costly. | • Have a qualified technician perform a full inspection, voicing, and regulation every 3–5 years.
• This includes checking the soundboard, bridges, and internal mechanisms. | | 10 | **Keep It Covered** | Dust, light, and insects can damage the interior. | • Use a breathable piano cover when the instrument is not in use.
• Avoid plastic covers that trap moisture. | ### Quick Checklist for Daily Use - **Before playing:** Check humidity, ensure the lid is closed, and wipe the keys lightly. - **After playing:** Let the piano rest for a few minutes, then wipe down the keys and lid. - **Monthly:** Inspect the action for smoothness, check for loose screws, and ensure the piano is level. By following these simple habits, you’ll preserve the piano’s tone, extend its lifespan, and enjoy a reliable instrument for years to come.
